title: Great marketing, worst app on the market
body: On social media, they make it seem like a well thought out dating app curated for Jewish singles. In reality, once you download it, they instantly make you pay by far the highest fee of any dating app to access the basic features, which is pretty much just a knock off of Hinge. To make matters worse, they still hide Most of the profiles behind a paywall undo the guise off “ we don’t wanna have you just endlessly scroll unlimited options” except you can for an added fee. So ultimately they choose 10 profiles to show you. And if you don’t like any of them too bad, you either have to pay them more or you have to wait hours to access the app again. So sad because conceptually this could have been good, but clearly it is being run by people pressed for cash. I want a nickel and dime every aspect. Developers there is a huge opportunity in the market to do this right

title: Fraudulent Behavior
body: Nice enough app interface - poor match quality and low interaction meter. Hosted an IRL event during which guests who paid $22 were instructed to meet up at a bar that was fully shut down and not in operation. Thus, in essence, we paid $22 to have someone make us a restaurant reservation - something we can easily do for free. It has been a week and they have yet to refund me $22 for a ticket to an event that was not remotely carried out as promised. I paid $20 for one month's subscription to the app - after several days of complete silence, I unsubscribed. Having paid, I still retained my 30-day usage period. Within this usage period, I bought a Boost for $9.99 to salvage what was left of the very underwhelming app. Rather than simply boost my account, LC debited me an extra $20 to resubscribe without my consent. Not only is this double dipping, as my account has already been paid through the month, but is egregiously bordering on theft. A slimy business practice overall to bring back customers who clearly have had dismal and underwhelming experience with this "dating app." Overall - completely hideous both virtually and in person. Save your money and avoid.

title: review I wish I saw before paying
body: If there were a dating app equivalent of a timeshare scam, this would be it. First, they reel you in with glossy ads full of impossibly attractive Jewish men who look like they stepped straight out of a JDate fantasy. Reality? Nearly every single guy is exclusively bald (nothing wrong with baldness, but don’t sell me on hair when it’s clearly a hat-free zone), and—bonus!—they live in entirely different states. You’ll spend more time calculating airfare than planning a date. Then comes the membership trap. You fork over a monthly fee thinking you’re getting the golden ticket. Nope. That “membership” buys you exactly seven swipes a day on people hundreds or thousands of miles away. Oh, and those “in-person events” they hype up? Not included. You have to buy another ticket to attend—so your membership is basically a cover charge for the privilege of paying more. This app is a catfish buffet with a paywall.

title: Don’t Waste Your Time
body: If you look up “Lox Club” on TikTok, the only recent videos you will see are from two individuals who are both related to the founder. You’d think that if this app was as exclusive and as ‘groundbreaking’ as its employees say, then the CEO wouldn’t need to ask his family members to pretend to be other people, and promote it just to get more people to try. If I can save even one person from being scammed in the same way that I did, then great. Don’t get me wrong, I’ve worked for startups for over half my life and I understand more than most people what it takes to make something out of nothing. I respect hustle, and I respect hard work. What I don’t respect is a blatantly dishonest marketing strategy and developers who claim every few weeks to have fixed the many bug issues the app has, just for that to be….yet another lie. You’re better off joining Hinge or Bumble (which are both free.99) instead of trying your luck on a service which was literally created with the intent of ripping you off, instead of helping you find love. I’m out.

title: Don’t waste your time
body: A BIG fat WASTE of time and money. The price is ridiculous for what you can do on the app. You get 5 people every 6 hours, sometimes less, most of whom are on the other side of the country (despite your location preferences) and are paid to be on the app. There is absolutely no quality control, you’ll see the same men on any other app. You’ll remain on a waitlist for any events, which should be avoided anyway. The ratio of women to men is absurd, they don’t care if 1 man shows up but 200 women do. If you’re accepted to an event you still have to pay for a ticket. They don’t answer your emails, any problem you have they’ll just give you a free “skip the wait”. I’m letting my subscription expire and deleting this app. The 10+ women I’ve met who use the app agree. Thanks to lox club for making Judaism seem like an elitist, exclusive, better than thou club.

There is a claim that people are vetted and waitlisted, etc. If people are vetted and the app is meant to be aimed towards Jewish people, why are there people ostensibly posting in their profiles that they aren’t Jewish? title: Don’t Do It
body: Please read the other bad reviews of which there are many. This is a total SCAM. They claim the app is different and exclusive. You have to be “vetted” but I have a feeling they just let everyone in. The interface is a replicate of all of the other swipe dating apps you’re familiar with, but it lets you swipe on about 5-10 people and then locks you out unless you throw down more money! They claim this is because you should take the time to read through everyone’s profile before making your swipe decision. You get a few more swipes the next day, but then after a few days I started getting people from all over the country. The app has a filter function but in chatting with the “matchmaker” I found out it doesn’t actually function. I live in Los Angeles and I have been getting folks who live in Georgia, NC, NYC. During a pandemic this seems ridiculous. My guess is that they don’t have a lot of members yet probably because it’s a play to pay app. I asked for a refund and they never wrote me back so I’m leaving my very first review for an app because I feel totally cheated. Lost $90+ on this. Wish it was cool but I’m EXTREMELY DISAPPOINTED.

title: Ridiculously High Standards
body: They label the app: “ for Jews with ridiculously high standards”. Unfortunately this Jew has high product and user experience standards. I’m in SF and received roughly 5 users in SF, followed by a couple in NY, and then LA. After maybe 15, I was asked to pay to see more users. I give them a break because they’re new, but bad user experience across the board loaded with bugs, antiquated usability, and it feels like a marketing-centric cash grab. Add some science to this thing- get a good product person- focus on proper customer acquisition- Grow your F-ing network first and then have the audacity to upsell. Your a brand new night club with no one inside and a supposedly long line to get in. Give your customers a reason to keep their subscriptions... and don’t pander to Jews- because, as you point out, we have higher standards

title: How much?!
body: They charge for everything, and when I thought I was signing up for the monthly $9 fee they charged me for the whole year! It’s pretty presumptuous that you assume anyone would use this app for that long. It just feels like a scam, the whole thing.

title: Same same
body: Legit the same as Hinge, except it’s somehow worse. Slim pickings, no way to pick location and can’t figure out why they were mentioned in the Times. 🤷🏼‍♀️

title: $30 for nothing
body: I’ve been on a it a week. You pay $30 for 3 months access with only the ability to swipe on 10 people a day. I’ve had 0 matches and I’m generous and swipe yes on everyone. Every account is a handsome successful guy who makes six figures which feels super sketchy to me. Dating apps should have a variety of people. I assumed they matched for you but it’s all whoever is on their data base. No impressed. Save yourself some $ and go on Jswipe or bumble.

title: One of the worst dating apps
body: Heard about it from a friend, seemed cool so i applied. I was accepted a few weeks later. It makes you pay $35 a month before even being able to check out the app. I did it thinking it may be worth it, big mistake!! What a scam! They show you 5 people and then make you pay $5 to see more people, insane. Also, total lack of functionality and no ability to adjust location proximity to the few people you are looking at. This app is taking the lame, greedy, tech start up dork to the next level of sleezy. Layering on the fake story and hyping it as if its actually “different” and not just a mechanism to make easy cash for the founders. Dont wast your time on this crap, so bad.

title: Rip off raya and hinge
body: Literally so underwhelming once accepted. Shows like 5 mediocre guys before making you wait hours to swipe through more. Plus you have to pay $12/month minimum

title: Doesn’t work
body: After diligently swiping, for over a week, I didn’t get a single match. I am using the same profile and pictures that are successful on other apps and I don’t have problems there... Agree with what others have said about the matchmaker being unhelpful and slow to respond. I really wanted to love this, but I’ve canceled.

title: Disappointing
body: Well, this app has certainly not lived up to my expectations in any way. It's no different then the other apps, frankly it's worse. I get like two people (who are usually nothing like I asked to be matched with nor do they even live on this side of the country) and then am told they don't have enough matches to meet my preferences. I also don't see how this is an app for "people with extremely high standards". (Sorry to say there are very few people I find remotely attractive and the profiles don't really give you much insight on a person) As my brother said, seems like a scam, that someone had a connection at the New York Times to get that article posted. Really disappointed, I was very excited about being approved and hoped it would amount to something more. Also glad I paid $4.99 for legitimately TWO more swipes. Y'all had a good idea... poorly executed. I most likely will NOT be paying for the service after my free trial. If I had paid for this I would insist on a refund.

title: Fake 5 star reviews
body: Someone writes in August they tried to get in “for years”. How is that even possible if it’s a new app?? I’m def not paying for an app where I can’t even see users. And then have to pay extra on top of that.

title: Yikes
body: Downloaded this app over a month ago and still have not gotten any matches. They’ve told me it’s a technical issue but then doubled back and said it was because their app is “different” and not for mindless matches. I asked for my money back and they wouldn’t give it to me. Major let down. DONT DOWNLOAD!!

title: Not as advertised
body: Price is absurd. Claim to be exclusive but let everyone in it seems. Doesn’t have any benefits at all. Oy Vey

title: This is not sustainable
body: I’ve never written a review of an app before. I do hope the app’s creators take the criticism to heart because I think it is a cool idea and has potential. As it is right now, the app is essentially a scam. You’re told it’s “exclusive,” that there’s a “long waitlist,” and that only “20%” of applicants are accepted.” This is effective marketing, actually - the aura of “exclusivity” makes you more likely to pay fees once you’re finally “accepted.” It is of course against their interest to deny anyone, because if they “accept” you, you must pay to use it. An app like this is only going to spread through word of mouth among Jewish circles, and I don’t know why anyone would recommend it to a friend right now. It is clearly not just for people with high standards - that becomes evident quickly. They limit the swipes you get then charge you for more (I guess it’s small, but still insane). In a vacuum, the app interface itself is pretty low quality and worse than any other dating app I’ve seen. The only novel feature, the matchmaker, is unresponsive and acts like they don’t want to help. I get that offering a free trial might expose the fallacy of “exclusivity,” but securing people’s short term payments does not outweigh the drawbacks of forcing people to pay for a service that just isn’t worth paying for at all. As it is right now, I don’t see this app lasting very long. Time to get back to the drawing board.

title: Gimmicky
body: I’m Jewish and my grandma wants me to find a nice Jewish boy. That said, she’s not as limiting as this Jewish country club of an app. It excludes people who don’t have the money to pay the membership fee.

title: Waste of money
body: I just joined the app but have been so disappointed- so much so that I’m writing my first review ever. First, with the quality of profiles. They just seems normal quality for a dating app as opposed to how they tout it as being exclusively for more ambitious people. They say they have a whole team review every applicant and that they only accept 20% but based on the profiles it seems to me like they accept...everyone. 100% of applicants. Their exclusivity branding feels like a sales gimmick. Yet perhaps most disappointing is that they have this feature where they only show you like 10 profiles before making you wait hours for more (a “new batch” they call it). They say it’s to make your scrolling more intentional but: 1) Please don’t tell me how to scroll. Are we children? 2) It doesn’t at all increase intentionality- knowing I only have 10 profiles I can see at a time doesn’t make me assess the profiles any less quickly or be any more open. This is because intentionality isn’t a function of technology—the opposite in fact—and cant be forced so using *technology* to *force* it definitely doesn’t work. 3) With it being national and with many regular ol’ profiles, it’s likely you’ll scroll through all 10 allotted profiles and not like anyone based on geography and quality not bc you’re not being open and need to slow down. 4) The very function of a dating app is breadth to then find depth with very few. Cutting off the breadth is beyond frustrating and really curtails and limits the experience. I don’t want to be in your app every few hours. I want to be on it whenever I have time for however long but when I can only see so few profiles it makes it hard. I therefore wonder if they offer such small “batches” because there are so few users they don’t you to run through everyone and not continue payment...and/or to make more money because you can “skip the wait” for $5. Overall: Save your money, join other free dating apps, select for Jewish ppl, and just expand to a larger geographic region and it’ll be better than this experience.

title: Not worth it
body: This app is a scam lol. They give no free trial (and make you pay for at least 3 months at a time), the buttons barely click, they show you approximately four people at once, sometimes who don’t live in your city, and then you have to pay $5 to see more people on top of the fee you’re already paying (or wait hours). And they threaten to cancel your account if you don’t do the membership (aka because they claim there’s a long waitlist). Terrible practice. Pay for hinge premium instead - money far more well-spent. Also - pretty sure most, if not all, of the positive reviews here are fake.

title: Don’t waste your money
body: Worst dating app. It’s definitely not exclusive, as it claims, and will only let you see a few people on the app every few hours. They say this is a way to reduce meaningless swipes, which I would have believed if they didn’t offer unlimited swipes to members for more money and/or mentioned this prior to purchasing the app. I’d like a refund.

title: Don’t waste your time with this beta
body: This app is far too early stage to be rolled out. It has no geography filter (a basic requirement), and their “matchmaker” option is a joke. They won’t actually make any difference in the matches you’re shown, and their service/help is limited. There’s no point in being on this app unless you’re in NYC or LA - or until Lox Club can do a halfway decent job and add a location filter. Hard pass, and certainly not the app for someone with “ridiculously high standards.”

title: Not What I was looking for
body: After paying for the subscription you don’t have control over location preference and only see a few potential matches ever couple hours. After using the app for 12 hours I reached out to cancel and get a refund on a 6 month subscription but they said they couldn’t. Terrible customer service move for a new-ish app

title: Not worth your time
body: Pointless and limited pool. Amateur staff.

title: The Lox Club as a Social Experiment
body: By making their members pay for their app, the Lox Club becomes an incredibly self-selecting app. I would never want to date someone who pays $10 a month on a dating app. Where do all those folks go? It’s getting rid of half your clientele right off the bat.

title: No diversity
body: Waste of time. Need a larger pool of more diverse folks. Want to get paired with the same ten people obsessed with Instagram? Go for it.

title: Waste of money
body: This app is such a scam. Do not waste your money or time on this!

title: Not enough people
body: You have to pay to see people in cities no where near you, and you’re also limited to seeing about 10 matches a day. Wish I could get my money back.

title: Wait to purchase
body: I wouldn’t spend your money on buying this app. They are too new and you get the same four matches over and over that you have already clicked “no” on. Additionally they give you matches that live on the opposite side of the country with no option to change that. While they build their community, they should offer free trials or a one month subscription offer at a very low rate.

title: WHAT A JOKE
body: The sign up process is super unfriendly and they put up obnoxious attitude when you contact them.

title: Elitist
body: No

title: not a big enough user base
body: getting matches in cities around the country/world, clearly not enough people using the app locally

title: Very disappointing
body: If you don’t live in NYC or LA, or if you’re not willing to start out as a long distance thing, this app is virtually useless. There were almost no potential candidates where I live (South Florida… but too far from Miami to date someone who lives there.) The app does not let you choose geographical location, so my feed was filled with people that were too far away to date.

title: Zero Location filtering!!
body: If you were trying to meet someone in your region, good luck the app does not really help with that . You literally cannot filter even by state ! If you want a great way to browse Jewish people from all around the world this is it!

While there’s an improvement on how the men look on this app, I found it personally to be a waste of money. Not only do you pay to be included, but you have to pay extra to see who likes you. Then you endlessly send likes in hopes to get a match and it never happens. Maybe it’s my luck, idk. I also hate how this app is advertised. It just feels more gimmicky than genuine connecting with anyone.

title: Very location dependent
body: Can’t set location presences. If you are NY, plenty of good profiles. Unfortunately if you are not, all you get is NY profiles.

title: Not useful
body: Every day this app shows me people in Delray Beach, FL, Baltimore, MD, London UK - I don’t live in any of these places. How is this useful?

title: It’s ok
body: Honestly there is no location feature and all these guys are great but you can’t search locally so that’s annoying

title: Overpriced waste of time
body: This app has hardly anybody on it, though they charge a premium price. Way overpriced when you can see pretty much the same and more people on hinge after you filter for Jewish. The high price is keeping people off the app. Who’s ever running this does not seem to have the intention to curate a large audience, but rather to make money off a few people that do join. I rarely write reviews, but I was thoroughly displeased. To sign up for a three month minimum subscription just to see anyone only to find out that there’s nobody to see.

title: Not worth the money
body: Very expensive and hardly shows anyone in my state. Keeps suggesting people from NYC when I live several hours from there, and almost every like I get is from someone I would need to hop on a plane to meet

title: Want to like, keeps freezing
body: Heard really good things and the IRL events are great. But I finally decided to get a membership and the app freezes everytime I open it. Def not worth it now. Super frustrating.
seems like another unabashedly gate keeping schema that runs this app. thanx

title: Not worth it
body: I was really hoping to get high quality matches after paying 50$ for a dating app.. after going through few matches, the app asks me to pay extra 4,99 to see more people which I did. But it’s just to show other few people and asks again for 4,99…. ? most of the people shown to me are not even located in my area ? I am not looking for a long distance relationship. This should have been properly stated. Also, the people shown are definitely not what I would go for. Very disappointed.

title: Feels superficial
body: I need deeper and spiritual connection. My heart does not fall on love with the career success of a partner or their hobbies.

title: Limited views and no location filter sucks
body: I get the limited views thing. Raya has it too, but theirs refresh every few hours. This literally feels like I get to see 10 profiles that live nowhere close to me and don’t get to see anybody else that day. 70% of the people I see live in NY. I live in DC. The events are nice. But it really doesn’t feel like they “prioritize finding local matches”. Raya targets rich and famous people who are more likely to have the means to travel and date abroad.

title: Only if you are in NY/LA or planning to move there
body: I didn’t mind waiting 6 hours even if the handful of options were no good, I do mind running out of options and showing me people in different cities I’ll never meet. If there’s slim pickings on JSwipe, there’s even less here. But hey, maybe I’ll get a few matches in the 6 month lock-in.

title: Support is the worst part
body: 1) If you’re an LGBTQ+ person, this app isn’t for you. You’ll see matches across the US, but I saw very few in my local area. I fought for a refund, which they gave (I had bought a gift subscription through their website, otherwise it would have been up to Apple’s lackadaisical refund system), but you can’t really set up a specific location with the app. They expect that someone in NY will want to meet someone in LA. 2) The events are fun but support is not forthcoming about details unless you repeatedly email them for help. I don’t have a problem paying for events, my issue is they don’t give details in a timely fashion unless you harass them. 3) Support is only over email. If you have a timely issue, good luck getting a reply.

title: Great idea, poor execution
body: Used the app for three months in NYC. Not worth the time and effort compared to Hinge. Signed up for a premium membership primarily to have priority access to in person events. Got accepted to the first event, and then none of the other eight. The app gives no indication of when an event sells out, leaving you in the dark if you should make other plans or not. For the first month, I received a reasonable number of matches. Starting month two, I did not receive a single match. This continued through month three. Support is generally unresponsive unless it’s about billing. I’d give the app another chance if the above issues could be fixed.

title: Strong concept, but limited reach and high cost make it tough to recommend broadly.
body: Lox Club is a niche dating app designed for Jewish singles, which is great if you’re looking to meet within the community. The prompts and questionnaires stand out—they’re well thought-out and make starting conversations easier and more fun. That said, there are a few downsides. The number of likes you can send is limited, and to get full access, you’ll need to pay for a fairly pricey membership. Matches can be few and far between, and unless you’re based in New York City, the user base feels pretty sparse.

title: No way to delete profile. 1 month free subscription link is dead.
body: App just seems shady with no way to self delete. I was also sent a free 1 month trial and the link is dead. The email support does seem responsive, but don't have faith in paying for a subscription without very basic UX features.

title: Broken Experience for a Paid Product
body: The app is showing outdated information—if it’s pulling old data from my profile, then I assume other profiles are stale too. Not sure where it’s caching data from, but it’s disappointing, especially for a paid membership. You expect this kind of thing to just work. Erodes trust.

title: Don’t use unless you live in NY
body: If you live in NY it’s moderately worth it. If you don’t, don’t bother. Over 80% of the people are based in NY and you can’t specify location preferences, so your 15 swipes a time are practically useless. Then you have to wait 6 hours to do it again

title: Can’t Filter By City
body: Can’t see people only in your city, can’t even see who’s liked you. App doesn’t really tell you how to use it. Wouldn’t recommend.

title: mediocre at best - i’m in a metro city and it’s recommending me people in a different state
body: UI is subpar, don’t have any users on the app, and way too many paywalls. Definitely better off using Hinge with the Jewish filter..

title: Not worth a penny
body: This app was designed with only those amongst us who are truly down bad in mind. A full refund would not go far enough in making up for the wasted time I spent on this app. Use hinge and filter to Jewish it’s free and far superior to anything offered by this middling-to-poor application.

title: Least useful dating app
body: The app features work, the product itself does not at all. You also can’t charge a high price point when you basically have no user base. Come on.

title: Big promise, super underwhelming
body: I will preface with this, you will find on paper the most attractive Jews. However, I’m in Los Angeles and they keep showing me people from New York and miami. Their new “matchmaker” feature is quite amazingly bad. You get to choose things that you love, things that you hate & based on that they will match you with someone. Twice in a row they offered me someone who literally had the things I LOVE on their HATE LIST. And lastly, the amount of non Jews on the app will surprise you.

title: App is terrible, events are ok
body: App is terrible, you’ll literally get the same people you would get on hinge but fewer of them and living really far away. Obvi not exclusive. The events are ok- but like ALL of the events have music playing at insane club volumes. Literally can’t hear a word anyone is saying. Not sure why they would do that at a dating event. Its so annoying to be yelling “hi where are you from?” On a Wednesday, I’m not trying to lose my voice mid work week. Also just fyi, Jewish is a heavily emphasis on “ish” even by Reform standards, they served bread on Passover and have basically no regard for the Jewish calendar in event planning.

title: Disappointing
body: Super disappointing app, I got matches for the week before I had to pay and then once I paid I didn’t get any matches. If I do, they don’t respond, and we don’t hear back about events either.

title: Don’t waste your money
body: Lox Club is a disappointment. I am deeply discouraged from using the app. The price is obnoxious for the apps capabilities. You’re best bet it to use hinge and filter on Jewish. There is a limited amount of people on the app and many of them are paid/ part of an ambassador program for being on the app. Also there are non- Jewish people on it, which defeats the purpose. The app will match you with people who are so far away that you will never be able to meet your matches. Not only is the app lack luster and a waste but the events are really bad. I attended the Miami event and everyone there was incapable of having a conversation. The event was at a random bar in the middle of nowhere and was hosted by someone who was flirting with every single man there (no hate). I made more quality connections with the females that attended. But it’s obvious that even an app where people are paying so much money to connect the problem with todays dating pool is not going away. All the men are either Andrew Tate fanatics or are seeking a booty call and all the women simply would rather be alone than deal with it. Don’t waste your money.

title: Just poorly designed
body: While the interface is fine. The fact that you have to pay money and it limits how many people you can see is below market standard and very discouraging. There also needs to be a feature where you can see people in your metro area only as unless you live in LA or New York. You just need up with barely any matches. Honestly just not worth the effort.

title: Do not download if you Live in Los Angeles
body: They do not have enough profiles in LA so they will start showing you ones in NYC, Florida, and Canada. I asked them why they do this, and their excuse is so you can meet people all over the world. But would anyone ever move across the world for someone they met on an app? I don’t think so. Save your money and spend it somewhere else. However if you live in NYC I do think this app works. Just not in LA

title: Only works if you’re in LA
body: At least it seems that way? I’ve almost exclusively only seen people that live in LA or greater California which is essentially useless to me as someone who lives in NYC. Feels like they should have a location preference because I like the idea but it’s a total waste of time when no one is in my area. Also they allow u the lowest amount of swipes I’ve ever witnessed on a dating app, especially given you’re already paying for it.

title: No algorithm
body: This app has no algorithm. It simply serves up everyone, in any city, within your age range. Useless. I’m in NY and received two entire batches of members in FL and CA. Why??

title: Just another app
body: The lox club is just another dating app out there that gives you the same quality of people from other dating apps except you have to pay for it. Not worth the money

title: Time to at a geofilter
body: I’ve been using this app for a little bit now, but when you only get around 10 moves every 6 hours and all of them are people from states plane rides away the app becomes less usable. I unfortunately will not be using this app again until a location setting is added. After a while it get aggravating that 1 out of every 20 people is sometime anywhere remotely close to you especially for something you must pay for in order to use.

title: Not Exclusive
body: Went through the whole process of being vetted, set up my profile, then at the end was asked to pay $36 fee for a 3 month subscription. Decided against it! Fast forward to a couple days later and I’m getting dms through Instagram from guys who have seen me on Lox Club?? Why is my profile up? I never subscribed to the service?? Also the men dm’ing me are definitely nowhere near the standards of what you would consider to be exclusive.

title: D grade Raya
body: Loved the concept of this and thought it might be Raya meets hinge - cool people with more substance. However, I’ve found the app to be very lacking. Few potential matches in my city (Los Angeles) and several of the live events they host that I’ve been too have been Terribly managed. They’ve also lacked good customer service. Overall, save your money and stay on Hinge or Raya or really anything else. Very disappointed.

title: Date people who live in New York City!
body: I live in LA...

title: What a Let Down
body: I’ll start this off by saying I was really excited about this app when I heard about it and think the concept is there. This is marketed as a dating app for Jews with impossibly high standards and I definitely fit the bill. They also market themselves as exclusive (claim to only accept 20 percent of applicants) and claim to put all applicants through some vetting process or some sort. I was definitely an early adopter of this app and hesitant to pay for a dating app. However, I was excited about the idea, told all of my friends, and convinced them to also purchase it. What a mistake. This app starts off kind of strong. The interface is clunky but the quality of potential matches was (initially there). You only get a couple options to swipe through before you run out and have to wait 6 hours to replenish those. I soon noticed that none of the guys were in the city I was in. I live in Chicago and most of the guys were in LA or NYC. On top of that, the matchmaker is unresponsive and doesn’t care to help. Also, I swipe through my matches and rarely get a match at that time. I often get a notification later that I matched with someone and what’s the fun in that. Lastly, the matches rarely message me first and also rarely messages back. Very weird app. The only idea I like is the no-screenshot rule. I also think the quality of people I’m seeing has gone down in the past month. Highly disappointed, waste of money, they need to get it together before I can recommend someone else spends their money on this.

title: Not worth spending money on
body: This app isn’t worth spending money on and I’m surprised they don’t have an option to try out a month without committing to 3 months. There aren’t many people in the Bay Area and should support some location preferences. I understand some are open to dating anywhere but as someone with a strong west coast preference, I have no interest in dating someone In New York or Florida. Lastly, of the limited app dating experience I’ve had in general, this is the least interaction I’ve seen. I’ve had many matches but zero responses or communication from men on here, and none of them have tried to message first either. Seems like a waste of money and time thus far. 2 stars here because the way they built profiles is good and I like how the app looks. The questions could use some more creativity though , they look like an exact copy and paste from hinge.

title: Disappointed
body: Really wanted to like this app because I’m sick of all the other ones. I see many reviews about it being best if you live in NY or LA, which makes sense. However, I do live in LA and all my potential options are usually in NY. The guys are super cute there but I’m not tryna move to the east coast. It’s super frustrating especially because we’re limited in how many people we get every 6 hours, so it just feels like a waste each time like we were lied to and cheated out of something. They really need a location filter option, I think that’s the biggest issue. They say they’re really exclusive and only accept 20% of applicants, but there inherently lies another problem— if they’re not accepting people, how can I have more options? Seems backwards. I really wanted to give this a try but very disappointed. Or LA has run out of potential NJBs. Could just be that. When I finally do have a match, no one messages or responds.

title: For LA/NYC
body: This app reminded me a lot of the league but the few matches I received were from all over the world. If you don’t live in LA or NYC chances are unlikely you’ll find many people within a reasonable distance. Definitely wasn’t worth spending any $$ on. I’d consider rejoining in the future if they expand a lot more.

title: Disappointing
body: I love the idea of this app but unfortunately it has not delivered. Like other reviewers have said, it has totally lost the “exclusive” vibe as I’ve now seen the same people I see on every other app. The biggest disappointment is that amongst the ~10 people I can see at a time, hardly any of them are in my city! I’ve written The Lox Club to ask about this, and the response I’ve gotten is just that they’re working on it. It honestly seems like they launched the app too soon, don’t have enough people on it, and haven’t figured out the kinks. Save your money for when it’s in a better place - I wish I’d done that but likely won’t renew my subscription after these first few months of being a member.

title: Not worth it!
body: The creators hype this app to make it seem cool and exclusive. Then you complete a profile (if accepted) and only then learn that you must pay to get an access to swipe. Most of the matches are not local (I’m in SF and would expect more matches in this area) and it just has a pretentious scam-like feel. Also I *highly doubt* only 20% of the people who apply are accepted. I’m giving it two stars because every once in a while a person that seems like a potential good fit in my area does appear.

title: The algorithm is off
body: I am someone who has no problem matching with a high volume of people on any other app but it’s been 2+ months of swiping and I still have yet to match with anyone...

title: Not great
body: If you’re looking for a vortex of 27 year old finance bros who aspire to go to burning man get this app. If not look elsewhere. There’s no form of questions to actually match you with potential suitors. I would rather hang out with Gil Faizon than be at the same house party with these guys.

title: Not quite there yet.
body: I have had this app for about a year now. Learned a lot of good things and bad things about the app. I hope this review helps you make your decision. The good: you need to “apply” to actually become a member. This is really a fancy way of saying you have protection against bots and they make sure you are the right criteria. The bad: not enough members because of the absurd 95.99 a year price. A monthly price should be available or at least a trial period of one month free. This would make people at least try the app without having to pay for the 3 month subscription. Major features are missing because of the lack of members, such as location based matching. Why am I getting members who live in LA when I live in NY? Makes no sense and in my opinion they do this as “filler” because there isn't enough members bear my location. I can pretty much say with confidence 95% of members aren’t active. Out of all time I spent on this app I have matched with maybe 5 people. 2 of which actually responded. They need notifications like other dating apps as a reminder to swipe. Any person who pays $95 dollars a year is likely working during the day and is busy constantly (like myself). A quick notification reminding members to swipe would do this app good. Their “napkin notes” is a good idea in theory but I think the font is extremely hard to read and sending a “napkin note” doesn’t put you higher in the algorithm like it should. You should be able to like individual prompts like other dating apps. Instagram connectivity should be removed from the app. Their “ambassadors” are no more then popular influencers that tell their friends. I have seen this on multiple occasions throughout the time I have spent on this app. I know there really isn’t much “good” I have to say. I am in the tech field so I know what is possible with this app and what they have to do to make it better. You have the information you need to make an informed decision now. I hope I have shed some light on this new an upcoming app. Hopefully in the future lox club changes their business objectives and makes this dating app as popular as bumble or hinge.

For its limitations on when deciding whether to like or pass on from a profile and the wait period as a result, it remains at a 4/5 stars. This is not to say that this is a bad feature; because the logic behind its implementation is clear, they don’t want it to be an endless, unemotional, detached, scroll game of ‘who can rack up the most matches in one sitting’. Which is commendable given that it makes one think of who they are going to like or not; however because the community is still growing, if you are not in LA or NY, you may find yourself with a batch of profiles outside your city and then having to wait for few hours for a new batch of profiles.
